# Independent audit: two-witness max sharing and actual depth

**PASS after one wording repair.** I read
`candidate 709f4ee1b13a1688`
in full and reran its updated checker: **98 exact checks PASS**.

The actual extreme anchored representations of `{-1,0,1,2}` are exactly
the four listed pairs. Starting with unit demands at bases zero and one,
the upward one-input recursion gives `(0,1,2,4)`; reversal gives
`(4,2,1,0)`. All four speed vectors, including their maximum and sum,
are convex sequences. Their eroded radius interpolations are therefore
concave and give actual convex bodies with precisely those integer
fibers.

The maximum's INTEGER fibers are the intersections of the two directional
families. The chosen linearly interpolated max fiber hull need not equal
their full ambient intersection: at base `z=1/2`, that intersection has
radius `1-3e/2`, whereas the chosen max hull has radius `1-2e`. The author
has explicitly repaired the wording. Every stated mixed measure, cap
cost and depth formula is unchanged.

At each of the two middle centers, retain the reflected copy of the
smaller outer interval inside the opposite inner interval. Every closed
containing halfspace captures at least half of this symmetric pair's
total mass, namely `2R`, plus at least the own half-length `r`. The
four displayed tilt-one caps realize `r+2R` and cover both middle
planes. The endpoint ordinary maxima are exactly `R`, by finite tilt
isolation. This proves the claimed global depths for ALL ambient
normals, including pure integer and closed-boundary cases; it is not a
cap sample or an inference from an upper cover alone.

The costs `24,28`, cap losses `10,11`, exact normalized comparison and
derivatives follow. Supporting statuses are essential: the original
outside supporting point in the opposite middle interval contributes
zero loss, while the inside-supported entire outer interval contributes
its full loss. The alternative tilt-one-half menu is genuinely critical
initially but loses only eight along the maximum path, so its normalized
first payment is negative. This establishes selected-menu dependence
on the SAME actual deformation, without denying its true descent.

The shared-speed correction is likewise an exact boundary identity;
it does not permit ignoring the captured part of the shared loss. No
universal paying selection or parity denominator bound is inferred.

## Added Section 6: maximum closure need not preserve descent

The later three-fiber addition also **PASS**es. I reran the enlarged
verifier: **112 exact checks PASS**. For each directional array, the
middle half-length `1-e` plus the smaller reflected endpoint pair of
length `2(1-2e)` gives the all-normal lower bound `3-5e`. A finite large
integer tilt isolates that smaller endpoint in each of the two opposite
continuous directions, attaining the bound and covering the middle
plane. Endpoint ordinary maxima are at most one and remain strictly
below it throughout the stated range. Thus both individual paths have
the exact strict normalized decrease (15).

For their maximum, the same raw maximum is divided by exactly twice
that value, giving (16). The family is centrally symmetric, consistent
with this exact half-depth. This is an actual failure of preserving
global descent under max merging, stronger than failure of one fixed
menu. It remains an above-target calibration and makes no OC claim.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
